headline: Micron agreed to pay Netlist $600 million over five years to license its memory technology and end their patent fights.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: confirmed deal, but a legal settlement between two firms.
importance_line: It ends a threat to Micron's memory sales, including chips used in AI servers, and pays Netlist $600 million, but its effect on prices or supply for users is not stated.
summary: American Bazaar reports, citing company disclosures released on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, that Micron will pay Netlist $30 million a quarter from late 2026 to the third quarter of 2031, $600 million in all, for a five-year worldwide licence to Netlist's memory patents, including server memory modules and high-bandwidth memory, and both sides will drop all legal cases. It adds that Netlist had won a $445 million jury verdict against Micron in Texas and had sought an import ban on some Micron memory chips.
notes: Seeking Alpha page blocked (403). Read American Bazaar; Reuters, Digitimes and PR Newswire headlines confirm the same deal.
